content: The study focused on nutritional assessment and growth monitoring within countries implementing the Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI) strategy. Dr. Karimen León Flández, a specialist in Preventive Medicine and Public Health, outlined the objectives of the survey, which included describing the methods of nutritional assessment and the characteristics of growth monitoring in IMCI countries. Methods: The survey was conducted between February and March 13, 2015, across six regions: AFRO (Africa), EMRO (Eastern Mediterranean), Europe, PAHO (Americas), SEAR (South-East Asia), and WPRO (Western Pacific). A questionnaire with eight questions was used to collect data on the following topics: 1. Updates to national IMCI chart booklets. 2. Nutritional assessment practices in IMCI. 3. Growth monitoring practices in IMCI countries. Key Findings: 1. Updates to IMCI Chart Booklets: Nineteen countries reported updating their national IMCI chart booklets based on the 2014 generic trial version. 2. Nutritional Assessment: 3. Defining Acute Malnutrition: Visible severe wasting was still utilized in 39 countries. 4. Growth Monitoring Programs: Thirty-nine countries reported having separate growth monitoring (GM) programs, which were often integrated with routine immunization services. 5. Age Groups for Growth Monitoring: Growth monitoring was most commonly performed in children aged 0–60 months. 6. 7. Coverage of Growth Monitoring: Data on the coverage of growth monitoring among children up to 12 months of age was available in 23 countries, while no data was reported for the remaining countries. Conclusions: Growth monitoring is predominantly conducted in children aged 0–60 months. Clinical signs, such as visible severe wasting, remain widely used for identifying acute malnutrition. Separate growth monitoring programs are present in many countries and are often integrated with routine immunization activities. Data on growth monitoring coverage is limited, with information available from less than half of the surveyed countries.
